newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Khaleda Zia blasts Bangladesh govt over India.
newsitem.headline: Khaleda Zia blasts Bangladesh govt over India.

text.p: Bangladesh's main opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia blasted the government on Friday for its "pro-Indian policies" and called on people to unite to protect national interests.

"The government (of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina) has been serving Indian interests more than of our own," she told an estimated 25,000 people at a rally organised be her Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) at Keshabpur in western Jessore dictrict.
"We must oppose the government's pro-Indian policies and resist any move to sell out national interests," she told the cheering supporters.

Khaleda criticised Hasina's eight-month-old government for "seeking to forge a subservient alliance with India by giving it a land corridor to send arms and troops to combat rebels in northeastern India, buying electricity from there and allowing free smuggling of Indian goods."
The government has repeatedly denied the charges.

"Farmers in Bangladesh are facing problems because they are not getting due price for their produce, including rice and jute, and the country may run into a famine in near future," the former prime minister warned.
Khaleda said law and order had "detoriated so much that people have no safety outside their homes and women are facing repression everyday.
"Police, and even the armed forces, are being made partisan," she said without elaborating.
"We must resist any oppression, repression and moral degeneration without any hesitation. This is our country and we must see to its good."
The BNP lost to Hasina's Awami League in a general election last June, and has often threatened to launch a countrywide campaign to topple the government.
"There is no similarity between the government's words and deeds. They loudly say about foreign investment flowing into the country but nothing like that is happening.
"The economy is faced with a disaster with foreign exchange reserves depleting fast and industries being closed for lack of supoort (from government)."
Khaleda said the BNP had offered to support the Awami League in its good work. "But I regret to say that they are doing nothing good where we can extend help," Khaleda said.
"Let there be no misgivings about our good intentions. We shall not accept or tolerate anything that goes against the people and the country."
